categories.main_business_segments: Ollie’s operates as a single business segment focused on retailing closeout merchandise and excess inventory. The company’s stores offer a broad assortment of brand name and private label products across categories such as housewares, bed and bath, food, floor coverings, health and beauty aids, books and stationery, toys, and electronics.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Ollie’s business model centers on opportunistic procurement, leveraging long-standing relationships with over 1,100 suppliers to acquire overproduced, overstocked, and closeout merchandise at deep discounts. The company augments branded closeouts with directly sourced private label goods and exclusive products, supported by scalable information systems for inventory, distribution, and store operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Ollie’s targets value-oriented consumers seeking bargains, with a core demographic of adults aged 25 and older. The company serves a broad customer base across socioeconomic groups, with over 80% of sales coming from its 14 million-member Ollie’s Army loyalty program.
categories.geographic_coverage: As of February 3, 2024, Ollie’s operated 512 stores across 30 contiguous states in the eastern half of the United States. The company continues to expand into new states and regions, with distribution centers in Pennsylvania, Georgia, Texas, and an upcoming facility in Illinois.
categories.supply_chain_position: Ollie’s operates at the downstream end of the retail supply chain, acting as a retailer that sources finished goods from manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, brokers, and other retailers. The company does not manufacture products but focuses on buying and selling closeout and excess inventory.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Ollie’s strategic priorities include expanding its store base, enhancing supplier relationships to increase access to brand name closeout deals, growing its private label assortment, and leveraging its Ollie’s Army loyalty program for targeted marketing. The company invests in distribution infrastructure, store remodels, and information technology to support scalable growth, but does not emphasize traditional R&D.
categories.revenue_model: Ollie’s generates revenue primarily through in-store sales of merchandise, with no e-commerce or omnichannel operations. The company’s revenue is driven by high inventory turnover, frequent new deals, and a treasure hunt shopping experience that encourages repeat visits.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Ollie’s competes with a fragmented group of discount, closeout, mass merchant, department, grocery, drug, convenience, hardware, variety, online, and specialty retailers. Its main differentiation is its focus on ever-changing brand name bargains at deep discounts, and it is often the first call for suppliers with closeout deals due to its scale and reputation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2023, Ollie’s reported net sales of $2.1 billion, up from $1.8 billion in 2022, with a five-year compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.5%. The company achieved net income of $181 million in 2023 and has grown its store base from 345 to 512 locations since 2019, targeting continued expansion toward a potential 1,300 stores nationwide.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Ollie’s delivers a unique value proposition of 'Good Stuff Cheap,' offering brand name and private label products at prices typically 20% to 70% below traditional retailers. The company’s treasure hunt shopping environment, witty branding, and high perceived savings foster strong customer loyalty and frequent visits, setting it apart from more conventional discount retailers.
